audit.whatIsWrong: Neither layer mentions Goes Where He Pleases. The whole page is built on 'land a Wallop stun into a wall-GNAR!' without saying that his passive resists the first immobilizing effect outright.
audit.why: Riot's text: Dr. Mundo resists the first immobilizing effect that hits him, losing health and dropping a cannister he can walk over to heal and reduce the passive's cooldown. So the first stun in any Gnar combo is absorbed — Wallop (7s) has to be spent as bait, and the wall stun from GNAR! is the one that must land second. Committing a full Rage bar into an unspent passive is how this matchup is lost.
audit.corrected: Passive named and sequenced in the cooldown block, the do's, the don'ts and the interactions report: spend Wallop to pop the cannister, then land the real CC.

audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers gave Gnar levels 1 through 5 and called the item stages even. The Dr. Mundo-side findings set the chart to Gnar, Gnar, Dr. Mundo, Dr. Mundo, Skill, Dr. Mundo, Dr. Mundo, and this page's own whys[2], whys[3] and whys[5] describe Mundo owning those stages.
audit.why: Infected Bonesaw (4s, 975 range, current-health damage) plus his passive regen erases Mini chip from 3 onward; his first drain-tank item out-sustains a Rage-gated burst; at 2+ items percent-health damage carves Mega bulk.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Gnar, Gnar, Dr. Mundo, Dr. Mundo, Skill, Dr. Mundo, Dr. Mundo on both layers, matching the mirror findings and the packet's Mundo-leaning stages.

audit.why: Mundo spikes at 6 (Maximum Dosage, flat 120s) and on his first drain-tank item; Gnar's spike is the loaded Rage bar, which spikes[1].when already labels 'Mega up' rather than pinning it to a level.
audit.corrected: No structural change; the first-item and 2+ item phase whys now say why they are his.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer calls his Q 'Infected Cleaver' twice (early and late). Riot's name is Infected Bonesaw.
audit.why: The kit file is authoritative on names and lists Q as Infected Bonesaw.

edits.before: Levels 1-2 are yours: Mini's ranged autos plus a single Boomerang Throw and the third-hit Hyper move-speed proc let you land a free trade Mundo's body can't answer before his sustain is online, and he has no dash to close on you. Catch the boomerang on its return for the cooldown refund and keep chipping the wave so he eats minion aggro every time he steps up to cleaver-last-hit. By level 3 it tightens — his Q (Infected Cleaver) casts and passive regen start healing your poke off, so stop trading for chip and only commit when Rage is climbing toward Mega.

edits.before: Late, the percent-HP truth catches up: his Infected Cleaver carves your Mega bulk regardless of armor, and Maximum Dosage makes him effectively unkillable in a straight duel while your form-locked burst plateaus. You don't win the 1v1 anymore, so stop trying — your value is the GNAR! engage in teamfights, flinging his squishies into a wall while your carries delete them. Push waves, take side objectives, and never let a full-build Mundo isolate you in Mini form on the map.

notes: The biggest gap on this page was Goes Where He Pleases: every all-in instruction here assumed a Wallop stun would land, and his passive resists the first immobilize outright. The page now sequences it — Wallop as the bait that pops the cannister, then the wall stun. Chart flips are one atomic group across both layers and follow the Dr. Mundo-side findings, so the two directions agree. His Q was named 'Infected Cleaver' in the content layer; the kit says Infected Bonesaw.
